meta.note: Plain-language explanations for readers who are new to the terms. They are summaries, not the legal definitions: the instrument named under 'See' governs.

terms.def: A recognised stock exchange. It lists equity, NCDs and commercial paper, runs an EBP for private placements and an RFQ platform for bond trades; NSE Clearing settles them.
A recognised stock exchange. It lists equity, NCDs and commercial paper and runs the BSEBOND EBP platform and an RFQ platform; Indian Clearing Corporation settles its trades.
An exchange recognised by the Central Government (now SEBI) under s. 4 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956. Its ownership and governance follow the SECC Regulations.

The agreement a listed entity signs with each exchange when it lists. It binds the entity to the LODR Regulations and the exchange's rules; breach can lead to fines, suspension or delisting under the SCRA.
A debenture that cannot be converted into shares. Privately placed NCDs of Rs 20 crore or more are issued through an EBP and listed within T+3 days of the issue closing.
NCDs, non-convertible redeemable preference shares and similar debt-like instruments issued and listed under the SEBI NCS Regulations, 2021.

A short-term unsecured money market instrument issued under RBI's directions. Listed CP follows SEBI's framework: listing on T+1 from receipt of funds, minimum lot of Rs 5 lakh, and no in-principle approval.
The exchange's approval of the draft offer or placement document before an issue opens. Needed for NCDs (not for CP) before the issue is put on an EBP.
The exchange platform on which private placements of debt of Rs 20 crore or more are bid and allotted. NSE's EBP and BSEBOND are the two exchange platforms.
An investor who commits in advance to part of a private placement on an EBP. The anchor portion is capped at 30%, 40% or 50% of the base issue depending on the rating.
A SEBI-registered intermediary (such as a merchant banker or broker) who bids on an EBP for its clients. Repeated client pay-in defaults bar it from bidding.
The option to keep subscriptions above the base issue size. On an EBP it may not exceed five times the base issue.
The code that identifies a security in the depositories. SEBI caps how many debt ISINs maturing in a financial year an issuer may have, to push re-issues into existing ISINs.
A fund each debt issuer deposits with the designated exchange, at 0.01% of the issue up to Rs 25 lakh. Debenture trustees draw on it to enforce security after a default.
The SEBI-registered trustee that holds security and acts for debenture holders. The issuer must send it periodic security cover and other reports on set timelines.
The value of the assets charged for secured NCDs compared with the amount outstanding. Certified quarterly to the trustee and the exchange.
A coloured meter showing the credit risk of a debt security, based on its rating. Required in offer documents, advertisements and online bond platforms from 21-11-2026.
The single quarterly filing (governance and financial parts) that replaced several separate LODR filings. Governance within 30 days of the quarter end; financials with the results.
The machine-readable format used for exchange filings. Regulation 50 prior intimations for listed debt are accepted only in XBRL since 01-12-2025.
The date that fixes who receives interest or redemption on listed debt. It is notified to the exchange in advance through the prescribed filing.
Disclosure to the exchanges of a default on a loan from a bank or financial institution that continues beyond 30 days, made within 24 hours of the 30th day.
A pledge, lien, non-disposal undertaking or similar arrangement over shares. Promoters disclose encumbrances, and reasons when they cross 50% of their holding or 20% of the company's share capital.
Fines the exchanges levy under SEBI's standard operating procedure for late or missed filings, per day or per instance, with escalation to freezing of promoter holdings and suspension.
Stopping trading in a company's securities for continuing non-compliance. Revocation needs payment of fines and compliance.
The exchange platform for negotiated secondary trades in corporate bonds and CP. Since October 2026 it settles on T+0 for trades up to 5 p.m.
A put option an issuer may offer retail investors in its debt, exercised through an exchange window at a price set from a rating agency's valuation.
A SEBI-registered broker that offers listed debt to investors online. Must display the Credit Risk-o-Meter from 21-11-2026.
A repo in corporate bonds in which the exchange's clearing corporation acts as the third party, managing collateral and settlement.
A SEBI-registered intermediary who manages an issue. Since October 2026 certain regulated, listed issuers need not appoint one for privately placed debt.
